_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: the conditional median is exactly 3 + 1.5 x treated + 0.05 x (age - 60)

agreement.claim: both engines report the same median effect, Hendricks-Koenker standard error, interval and age slope
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten significant digits on every key, including the standard error, from R's simplex and scipy's HiGHS solving the same linear program. harness/flexible_examples.test.py checks the estimate against statsmodels' iterative QuantReg, checks optimality by perturbation, and shows least squares estimates a different effect (1.66).

recovery.claim: the median effect and age slope are close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: Measured by harness/flexible_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99 of this generator.
